$$

Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $3$rd column.

The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are the pivot columns of $B?$

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Select all that apply.
before.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

before.:question/problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}?
$$

Select all that apply.
before.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.
